'''Qube Cinema Technologies''' is an Indian company operating in [[film]] and [[television]] technology. It provided digital non-linear editing and digital cinema sound to the Indian market in the 1990s. The company then began work in digital cinema products and deployment during the early years of the century.

==History==
Started in 1986 as Media Artists Pvt. Ltd. in [[Chennai]] (then [[Madras]]), India, the company was renamed to Real Image Media Technologies Pvt. Ltd. in the early 2000s after the merger of Real Image Pvt. Ltd. and JS Films into Media Artists Pvt. Ltd. Media Artists continued to be a brand of the company's audio post-production facilities until early 2017 but the primary focus of the company then moved to [[digital cinema]] and as of January 2018, the company's Qube digital cinema systems were installed in about 3760 screens in India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qubecinema.com/qube-all-india-theaters-list|title=Qube Indian Theatre List|date=Jan 2018|website=Qube Cinema}}</ref> In 2017, the company was renamed to Qube Cinema Technologies Pvt. Ltd. and in November 2017, it announced the signing of a definitive agreement to merge with [[UFO Moviez]] Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vccircle.com/pe-backed-ufo-moviez-qube-cinema-to-merge/|title=PE-backed UFO Moviez, Qube Cinema to merge|date=2 November 2017|website=VC Circle}}</ref> but after significant procedural roadblocks in the process at the [[NCLT]] Mumbai, the merger was called off in early 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/ufo-moviez-qube-cinema-merger-hits-nclt-roadblock/articleshow/68039137.cms|title=UFO Moviez, Qube Cinema merger hits NCLT roadblock|last1=Laghate|first1=Gaurav|date=2019-02-17|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-07-08|last2=Das|first2=Saikat}}</ref>

The first technology the company brought to India was computer-based non-linear editing with the [[Media Composer]] editing system from [[Avid Technology]] in 1993.<ref name="IndianExpress">{{cite news | url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/oldStory/78409/ | title=Cinema of the future is here, now | newspaper=Indian Express | date=19 September 2005 | first=Jaya | last=Menon | access-date=6 November 2018 }}</ref> Subsequently, the company brought digital cinema sound to India in a partnership with [[DTS (sound system)|DTS]] in 1995.<ref name="IndianExpress" />

In 2005, the company launched its own digital cinema system under the brand name Qube.<ref name="Screen">[http://www.screenindia.com/old/20001201/film6.htm Real Image Media Technologies Unveils Digital Cinema - Screen]{{dead link|date=November 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Qube Cinema, Inc. was set up in the US as a subsidiary of Real Image Media Technologies and markets the digital cinema technology of the parent company worldwide.<ref name="Span">[http://span.state.gov/wwwfspmarapr0754.pdf When Every Show Feels Like a Premiere - Span Magazine] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111016060255/http://span.state.gov/wwwfspmarapr0754.pdf |date=2011-10-16 }}</ref>

Qube Cinema was originally founded by Jayendra Panchapakesan and Senthil Kumar to sell and support technology products for the broadcast and cinema industries in India.<ref name="span.state">When Every Show Feels Like a Premiere - {{cite web|url=http://span.state.gov/wwwfspmarapr0754.pdf|title=Archived copy|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111016060255/http://span.state.gov/wwwfspmarapr0754.pdf|archive-date=October 16, 2011|access-date=November 3, 2011}}</ref> Qube Cinema has 7 offices across India and a subsidiary in Los Angeles, Qube Cinema, Inc. The Qube product line is established globally, with about 7,000 installations across 48 countries so far and has digital cinema operations in 4,000 cinema screens across India. In August 2011, Qube provided servers and technical support for the fourth year to the [[Venice Film Festival]].<ref>Qube Cinema Serving the Venice Film Festival - http://www.live-production.tv/news/cultural-events/qube-cinema-serving-venice-film-festival%C2%A0.html</ref>

In March 2011, Qube introduced a 4K integrated media block (IMB) that is Ethernet-based, allowing exhibitors to have their storage servers within or outside of their theater.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dager |first1=Nick |date=April 13, 2011 |title=Getting Down to Business: CinemaCon 2011 |url=http://www.digitalcinemareport.com/node/2353 |access-date=December 8, 2019 |website=Digital Cinema Report |archive-date=25 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425060512/http://www.digitalcinemareport.com/node/2353 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It allows for central storage in multiplex theatres and is designed to work with any digital projection system that supports an IMB. In September 2011, Qube introduced QubeMaster Xpress 2, for digital cinema mastering.<ref>Debra Kaufman, Creative Cow - http://magazine.creativecow.net/article/qube-cinema-showcases-digital-cinema-products-at-ibc {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130521044224/http://magazine.creativecow.net/article/qube-cinema-showcases-digital-cinema-products-at-ibc |date=21 May 2013 }}</ref>

Starting in 2012, Qube Cinema began installing its d-cinema servers and IMBs in Giant Screen theaters. In January 2012, Qube held the first public demonstration of 4K 3D streaming from a single server when they installed a d-cinema system at the [[Moody Gardens]] MG 3D Theater in Galveston, Texas.<ref>"Laser Focus", by Andreas Fuchs in Film Journal International - http://www.filmjournal.com/filmjournal/content_display/news-and-features/features/technology/e3i7cfb89cd186864c3e7d84318f2b402f9</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2012/scene/markets-festivals/tech-news-and-notes-4-1118049142/|title=Tech news and notes|last1=Caranicas|first1=Peter|date=January 24, 2012|website=Variety|access-date=December 8, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2012/digital/columns/biz-wide-eyed-over-narrowcasting-1118048828/|title=Biz wide-eyed over narrowcasting|date=January 19, 2012|website=Variety|access-date=December 8, 2019}}</ref> The transition of the [[Moody Gardens]] theater from 70 mm film to digital 3D used a [[Barco NV]] projector and Qube XP-I server and Xi IMBs. This installation was followed, in March 2012, by one at the [[Houston Museum of Natural Science]], which became the first commercial installation of the Qube Cinema single-server 4K 3D system when it upgraded the museum's Giant Screen Theatre from 70 mm film to digital cinema.<ref>Qube Cinema Delivers 4K 3D from a Single Server - {{cite web|url=http://www.ita-usa.com/?p%3D861|title=Archived copy|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927021652/http://www.ita-usa.com/?p=861|archive-date=September 27, 2013|access-date=July 27, 2012}}</ref> And, in October, Qube Cinema partnered with Global Immersion to install its d-cinema system at the Giant Screen theatre of the Peoria Riverfront Museum.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://news.creativecow.net/story/870068 |title=CreativeCOW |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=19 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819215637/http://news.creativecow.net/story/870068 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In May 2012, Qube introduced server software capable of synchronizing multiple IMBs, making 4K 3D projection possible for theatre owners.<ref>[https://archive.today/20130119061214/http://www.boxoffice.com/statistics/news/2012-05-14-qube-cinema-demos-multi-imb-synchronization-imb-supported-laser-projection-and-hfr-3d-at-cinemacon-2012 Qube Cinema Demos Multi-IMB Synchronization -]</ref> In August 2013, Qube partnered with D3D Cinema to install its single-server True 4K 3D system at the newly renovated Air Force Museum Theater at the [[National Museum of the United States Air Force]].<ref>Qube Cinema True 4K 3D System Installed for Giant Screen at Air Force Museum Theater - http://news.creativecow.net/story/872234 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130817065240/http://news.creativecow.net/story/872234 |date=17 August 2013 }}</ref> In January 2014, Qube Cinema released software updates that added support for [[Dolby Atmos]] surround sound <ref>Qube Cinema Servers to Add Dolby Atmos Support - http://www.btlnews.com/news/qube-cinema-servers-to-add-dolby-atmos-support/</ref> as well as Barco [[Auro 11.1]] sound<ref>Qube Cinema Adds Support for Auro 11.1 by Barco Sound System - http://www.broadcastbeat.com/index.php/qube-cinema-adds-support-auro-11-1-barco-sound-system/</ref> to its flagship XP-I and XP-D servers.

In November 2014, the company was listed by [[iSPIRIT]] (Indian Software Product Industry Roundtable), a non-profit think tank, in its top 30 index of Indian software product companies.<ref name="techinasia.com">[https://www.techinasia.com/top-30-indian-b2b-companies-total-market-cap-6-billion/ Top 30 Indian B2B software product companies with total market cap over $6 billion]</ref>

Apart from providing digital cinema in India and selling the Qube digital cinema technology worldwide, the company also masters Indian feature films into the digital cinema format.<ref name="Createasphere">[http://www.createasphere.com/En/insider-view/2359-growth-in-indias-digital-cinema-industry-part-2.html Growth in India's Digital Cinema Industry – Part 2<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

Intel Capital, the venture capital arm of [[Intel Corporation]],<ref name="EcoTimes">[http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/articleshow/1561733.cms Intel arm buys stake in Chennai's Real Image - The Economic Times<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> [[Nomura Holdings|Nomura]], the Japanese bank,<ref name="Variety">[https://www.variety.com/article/VR1117990001?refCatId=19 Real Image sees funds from Nomura - Variety]</ref> and StreetEdge Capital, a U.S. based investment partnership, were amongst the investors in Qube Cinema Technologies.

==EPIQ==
EPIQ, launched in 2019, is an Indian premium-large-format (PLF) system that competes with [[IMAX]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023 |title=Products – EPIQ |url=https://www.qubecinema.com/products/epiq |website=Qube Cinema}}</ref> The auditoriums use Barco 4K RGB laser projection, Dolby Atmos immersive sound and a 1.89-to-1 wall-to-wall screen; selected Indian and Hollywood titles are re-mastered in 4K specifically for the format.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asian Cinemas and Qube Cinema to expand footprint of EPIQ Premium Large Format across South India |url=https://www.qubecinema.com/news/asian-cinemas-and-qube-cinema-expand-footprint-epiq-premium-large-format-across-south-india |date=21 June 2024 |publisher=Qube Cinema}}</ref>

As of July 2025 the following EPIQ sites are in regular operation:<ref name="TOI2019">{{Cite news |title=Chennai company comes up with large-screen format with higher-lumens DCI projector in 1.9 flat ratio |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/tamil/movies/news/chennai-company-comes-up-with-large-screen-format-to-rival-imax/articleshow/70975002.cms |work=The Times of India |date=4 September 2019}}</ref><ref name="Herald2023">{{Cite news |last=Gowtham |first=G. |title=India's 2nd Largest Screen Opened in Tamil Nadu |url=https://www.indiaherald.com/Movies/Read/994605696/Indias-nd-Largest-Screen-Opened-in-Tamil-Nadu |work=India Herald |date=7 July 2023}}</ref><ref name="Palaxi2024">{{Cite web |title=Grand Inauguration: Palaxi Cinemas Unveils First-Ever EPIQ Cinema Screen at HiLITE Mall, Calicut |url=https://hiliterealty.com/grand-inauguration-palaxi-cinemas-unveils-first-ever-epiq-cinema-screen-at-hilite-mall-calicut/ |publisher=HiLITE Realty |date=25 January 2024}}</ref><ref name="Radiance2024">{{Cite news |title=Qube and Radiance Cinema launch EPIQ – Premium Large Format Cinema in Madurai |url=https://www.businessminutes.in/2024/09/qube-and-radiance-cinema-launches-epiq-premium-large-format-cinema-in-madurai.html |work=Business Minutes |date=2 September 2024}}</ref><ref name="Vetri2025">{{Cite web |title=Vetri E-Square: First Ever Dual EPIQ Screens |url=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/vetri-e-square-first-ever-dual-epiq-screens-raghav-t-0hbsc |publisher=LinkedIn Pulse |date=April 2025 |access-date=6 July 2025}}</ref><ref name="Hans2023">{{Cite news |title=Allu Arjun's 'AAA Cinemas' inaugurated in Hyderabad |url=https://www.thehansindia.com/cinema/tollywood/allu-arjuns-aaa-cinemas-inaugrated-in-hyderabad-803329 |work=The Hans India |date=16 June 2023}}</ref>
* '''V EPIQ''', Sullurpet, Andhra Pradesh – inaugurated 29 August 2019 and billed as the largest screen in South Asia.<ref name="TOI2019" />
* '''Broadway Megaaplex''', Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu – opened 3 July 2023 and is the largest screen in the state.<ref name="Herald2023" />
* '''Palaxi Cinemas''', Kozhikode, Kerala – Kerala’s first EPIQ auditorium, opened 25 January 2024.<ref name="Palaxi2024" />
* '''Radiance Cinema''', Madurai, Tamil Nadu – 50 ft × 27 ft “R-EPIQ” screen launched 2 September 2024.<ref name="Radiance2024" />
* '''Vetri E-Square''', Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu – India’s first multiplex with two EPIQ auditoria (65 ft × 34 ft and 61 ft × 32 ft), soft-opened January 2025.<ref name="Vetri2025" />
* '''AAA Cinemas''', Hyderabad, Telangana – houses the first '''EPIQ Luxon''' direct-view HDR LED screen (Screen 2), inaugurated 16 June 2023.<ref name="Hans2023" />
* '''ART Cinemas''', Hyderabad, Telangana – the state's first EPIQ auditorium, opened July 31, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=K |first=Manaswini |date=2025-07-28 |title=ART Cinemas: Ravi Teja's 1st Ever Premium Multiplex |url=https://www.m9.news/movienews/ravi-teja-launches-art-cinemas-in-vanasthalipuram/ |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=M9.news |language=en-US}}</ref>

The EPIQ roadmap includes ten screens across Telangana and Karnataka under a 2024 partnership with [[Asian Cinemas]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asian Cinemas and Qube Cinema to expand footprint of EPIQ Premium Large Format across South India |url=https://www.qubecinema.com/news/asian-cinemas-and-qube-cinema-expand-footprint-epiq-premium-large-format-across-south-india |date=21 June 2024 |publisher=Qube Cinema}}</ref>

===EPIQ Luxon HDR LED===
EPIQ Luxon adapts the PLF branding to a direct-view LED cinema wall that meets emerging DCI HDR brightness and contrast targets. The first installation opened in June 2023 at AAA Cinemas, Hyderabad, and is currently the only commercial LED screen in South India that operates under a PLF label.<ref name="Hans2023" />

==Qube Wire==
Qube Wire is the company’s cloud-based distribution and [[key delivery message|KDM]] platform. It was commercially launched at CinemaCon 2017,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Qube Cinema to showcase Qube Wire DCP Delivery Service at CinemaCon 2017 |url=https://www.boxofficepro.com/qube-cinema-showcase-qube-wire-dcp-delivery-service-cinemacon-2017/ |work=Boxoffice Pro |date=27 March 2017}}</ref> offering global KDM automation and optional electronic or hard-drive delivery of [[Digital Cinema Package|DCPs]].  

* '''Scale''' – By early 2025 the network served ‘‘over 5,000’’ cinemas in 51 countries following Qube Cinema’s acquisition of US-based MetaMedia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Qube Cinema Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire MetaMedia |url=https://www.dcinematoday.com/dc/pr?newsID=6400 |publisher=DCinemaToday |date=6 July 2025}}</ref>  
* '''Coverage''' – Prior to the deal the service already delivered content to 135 countries and generated more than 2.3 million KDMs annually.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Qube Wire – Home |url=https://www.qubewire.com/ |access-date=6 July 2025 |publisher=Qube Wire}}</ref>  
* '''Notable uses''' – Qube Wire handled the global, sub-one-week distribution of the multi-version blockbuster ''Baahubali 2'' (2017), sending ~200 GB packages to dozens of territories via its peer-to-peer mesh.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A New Ecosystem: Qube Wire Streamlines Delivery of Digital Content |url=https://www.qubecinema.com/news/new-ecosystem-qube-wire-streamlines-delivery-digital-content |date=2017 |publisher=Qube Cinema}}</ref>

The platform is accessible to distributors through a web dashboard and REST API, while exhibitors can ingest content via a lightweight theatre appliance or direct network transfer.
